subject: Request: Temporary SLA deviation & mitigation runbook — Stratix (DEAL-4521)
messages:
From: Carolyn Diaz <carolyn.diaz@stratix.io>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Tim Hooper <tim.hooper@stratix.io>, procurement@stratix.io
Date: Mon, 05 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected P1 incidents during maintenance — request for temporary SLA deviation

Hi Rishi,

Quick note from our ops team: during last night's edge maintenance window we saw intermittent P1s affecting inference latency for ~40 minutes in US-WEST. The customer impact was visible in production dashboards and triggered our on-call twice. We've attached the incident summary.

Stratix is asking for two things:
- A temporary relaxation for the formal P1 response window to allow for scheduled maintenance overlap (proposed: move from 15m to 45m for the next 72 hours).
- Confirmation of the runbook and escalation contacts we should use if issues recur.

We know this is a special-case ask because the maintenance ran into a datastore reindex; our legal/procurement team needs a short note from Redwood confirming the temporary deviation and whether any service credits will be applied if there is further impact.

Can you confirm next steps and who will own the runbook?

Thanks,
Carolyn Diaz
Head of Platform Reliability
Stratix

Attachments: incident_summary_20281105.pdf (PDF, 88KB)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Carolyn Diaz <carolyn.diaz@stratix.io>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Nov 2028 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected P1 incidents during maintenance — request for temporary SLA deviation

Hi Carolyn — thanks for the heads up and for the clear ask + incident summary. Appreciate the incident detail.

We can support a temporary deviation but want to formalize the scope and controls before approving:
1) Duration: 72 hours (we can sign off on Nov 5 09:00 PST -> Nov 8 09:00 PST)
2) Scope: apply only to the scheduled maintenance window (US-WEST edge) and only for P1 latency-triggered alerts that are directly tied to the maintenance activity.
3) Mitigation: Redwood will provide a dedicated escalation path with an augmented on-call (two-person backup) and an ops runbook we will share.
4) Credits: we'll provide an SLA credit cap if we miss agreed criteria — Priya, can you draft the runbook + a credit estimate?

Carolyn: can you and procurement confirm the bill-to entity and whether DocuSign is required for a short amendment? If so we can route a one-paragraph amendment for signature.

I'll keep this to a single-thread; Priya will follow with the runbook + proposed contact matrix in the next message.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Nov 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected P1 incidents during maintenance — request for temporary SLA deviation (runbook draft)

Rishi / team — draft runbook & mitigation plan below. I kept it concise so Stratix can consume quickly. Attaching a PDF and a preliminary credit estimate.

Summary: temporary SLA deviation for US-WEST maintenance window, 72 hours, with conditions and automated guardrails.

Runbook highlights:
- Activation: automatically active for maintenance window with start/end timestamps; Redwood SRE to toggle via console.
- Response posture: primary on-call (SRE-A) + backup on-call (SRE-B) for P1s; backup must acknowledge within 10 minutes if primary is paged.
- Escalation path: SRE-A -> SRE-B -> On-call manager (Marissa Cole) -> Rishi Malhotra. Phone and Slack escalation + PagerDuty.
- Containment steps: divert new heavy-batch traffic to warm pool, enable prefix-cache flush only when safe, scale inference pool by +20% (if capacity available).
- Communication: Redwood will post incident updates to Stratix slack channel every 15 minutes during active incidents; post-incident RCA within 48 hours.
- Credit approach: if a P1 occurs outside the covered maintenance condition within the 72-hour window (i.e., not maintenance-related), Redwood will apply a prorated credit. If the P1 is maintenance-related and within agreed window, no credit. See attached estimate.

Attachments: sla_deviation_runbook_v1.pdf, sla-credit-estimate-DEAL-4521.xlsx

Next steps (proposed):
- Carolyn to confirm bill-to and whether an amendment (DocuSign) is required.
- Ben to schedule the two-person backup shift (Ben, please confirm names & overlap).
- Marissa to be the escalation manager on-call for this window.

Ben — can you confirm backup names and that we have capacity to scale +20% in US-WEST during the period?

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Director, Customer Operations
Redwood Inference

(On priorities: this is tactical; please keep threads tight and only escalate to me if capacity or legal/contract language is required.)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Carolyn Diaz <carolyn.diaz@stratix.io>, Tim Hooper <tim.hooper@stratix.io>, procurement@stratix.io
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Nov 2028 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Approved: Temporary SLA deviation & runbook (Stratix — DEAL-4521)

Carolyn / Tim / procurement team —

Thanks for working with us on this. Per the internal review and the runbook Priya drafted, Redwood approves a temporary SLA deviation under the following conditions:

1) Window: 2028-11-05 09:00 PST -> 2028-11-08 09:00 PST (US-WEST maintenance only).
2) Scope: applies only to latency-triggered P1s that are demonstrably caused by the scheduled maintenance activity.
3) Controls: Redwood will have augmented on-call coverage (primary + backup) and will push incident updates to your Stratix slack channel every 15 minutes while incidents are active.
4) Credits: Redwood will not apply credits for incidents validated as maintenance-related and within the approved window. For any unrelated P1s during the window, a prorated credit will apply as per the attached estimate.
5) Amendment: if procurement requires signatures, please sign the one-paragraph amendment at the DocuSign link below; otherwise this email will act as the formal confirmation.

DocuSign (optional): https://docusign.com/templates/REDWOOD-SLA-AMEND-DEAL-4521
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/4521

Ben / Marissa: confirm that the two-person backup shift is scheduled and that we have the +20% scaling rule enabled for US-WEST. Once confirmed I'll send a short note to procurement with the credit attachment and close the loop.

Thanks again — we will follow up with post-incident RCA within 48 hours.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sla_deviation_runbook_v1.pdf, sla-credit-estimate-DEAL-4521.xlsx
